findings.text: TPM version one digest capacity is twenty bytes and the generic command buffer capacity is four thousand ninety six bytes.
TPM2 maximum digest extent equals the SHA512 digest extent, maximum name extent is that digest extent plus two bytes, null name extent is thirty four bytes, and maximum PCR bank count is eight.

Capability property identifiers are partitioned into fixed and variable ranges; the variable base is twice the group base with permanent, startup clear, handle counts and availability, counter, algorithm set, curve, lockout, recovery and audit properties at sequential offsets zero through twenty, while the fixed tail occupies offsets forty four through forty six.

PCR read response begins with update count and selector count, followed by hash algorithm, selector size, selector bytes sized by a minimum constant, digest count, digest size and a trailing variable digest area, tightly packed with multibyte integers in network order.

Random response pairs a size with a random byte area sized by a maximum constant, and capability response carries a more data flag plus subcapability, property count, property and value fields, both tightly packed with multibyte integers in network order.

PCR selection holds a hash algorithm plus selector size and three selector bytes, and context holds a sequence number plus saved handle, hierarchy and blob size, both tightly packed with multibyte integers in network order.

Algorithm registry assigns zero to error, four to SHA1, six to AES, eight to keyed hash, eleven to SHA256, twelve to SHA384, thirteen to SHA512, sixteen to null, eighteen to SM3 256, thirty five to ECC and sixty seven to CFB.

Locality identifiers run zero through four for static root of trust measurement, dynamic OS, dynamic root of trust environment, auxiliary components and CPU establishment, with four also serving as the maximum.
Bank description holds three sixteen bit values identifying the algorithm, the digest length and the kernel crypto identifier.
Maximum hashes per operation is five and command header size is ten bytes.

Digest entry pairs a sixteen bit algorithm tag with a digest area sized by the maximum digest constant and is tightly packed; command header carries a sixteen bit tag and thirty two bit length plus a thirty two bit union holding either command code or return code, with multibyte fields in network order.

Basic and extended accounting accumulation plus integral update, CPU time accounting and integral clearing are provided as empty inline helpers that accept task with namespace or statistics pointers and perform no action in this configuration.

Header provides compile time checks for exact type compatibility, function assignability to a type and pointer dereferenceability, each evaluating true on success, plus a bitmap declarator that sizes an unsigned long array from a bit count.

Each header defines a unique inclusion guard macro to prevent double inclusion, including guards for task accounting, type checking, base types, statistics synchronization, user access and for size related aliases.

Device, file set, inode, mode, link count, offset, process, address, key, timer, clock, message queue, user and group identifiers alias their kernel internal counterparts, with short mode as unsigned short and boolean as native boolean and pointer sized integers as unsigned long and long.

Fixed width and legacy aliases cover eight through sixty four bit signed and unsigned integers plus one hundred twenty eight bit integers, file offsets, sizes, pointer differences, clocks, addresses, short character and integer shorthands, and time, sector and block counts with specified widths.
Read direction is zero and write direction is one; page offset is unsigned long; DMA and physical addresses each have sixty four bit and thirty two bit variants selected by configuration.

Allocation, slab, file mode, block mode and operation flag types are distinct bitwise unsigned integers; sixty four bit aligned variants alias architecture aligned base types; kernel time is signed sixty four while sector and block counts are unsigned sixty four.

Atomic integer wraps an aligned integer counter and atomic sixty four wraps a signed sixty four counter, with a constant initializer for the former; reference count wraps the atomic form with an initializer that stores one less than the requested value.

Doubly linked list node holds next and previous self pointers; hashed list head holds first node pointer while node holds next plus pointer to previous next field; physical vector pairs an address with a length and resource size aliases physical address; hardware IRQ number is unsigned long.

Callback head holds a next pointer and a function taking the head itself and is aligned to pointer size with an alias for RCU use; deferred free heads exist in single link and RCU head forms; RCU wait holds an RCU protected task pointer; file system status holds free blocks, inode count with configuration dependent width, and two six byte name arrays; coverage handle holds a sixty four bit value only when enabled.

Callback signatures include RCU completion taking a head, RCU submit taking head plus completion, sized swap with and without private context, and comparison returning integer with and without private context.

Synchronization object is empty on sixty four bit word size and holds a sequence counter otherwise; counter object wraps a per CPU sixty four bit integer in one configuration and a plain sixty four bit integer in the other.

Helpers provide counter read, array copy with length multiple check, assignment, subtraction, synchronization initialization and fetch begin plus retry; one configuration uses per CPU atomics with trivial fetch that never retries, the other uses plain accesses with sequence counter initialization and sequence protected fetch.

On thirty two bit word size, initialization prepares the sequence object and readers bracket counter reads with begin and retry, repeating when retry reports contention; on sixty four bit both operations are trivial and never request repetition, with outer wrappers delegating to the inner variants.

Address untagging is identity in this configuration, with remote variant asserting the memory map lock is held before delegating; masked access capability is configuration dependent with a predicate reporting availability, read and write begin aliasing a common begin when available and yielding null with identity masking otherwise, plus combined read write aliases.

Checked copy from and to user returns the count of bytes not transferred, allows faults on entry, reports full length when failure is injected, and the from direction zeroes the trailing portion that was not copied; short aliases map to the inline forms.

Inatomic copy helpers forbid faulting context, apply instrumentation and object size validation around a raw transfer and return the uncopied remainder, with the to direction also honoring injected failure; a nontemporal from variant selects masked addressing when available or validates accessibility otherwise before delegating to the inatomic path.

Checked from helper requires either masking support or a successful accessibility check before transfer and orders validation against later side effects to resist mispredicted checks; its failure path zeroes the remainder to avoid exposing kernel memory.

Per task page fault disable nesting is a counted flag with paired increment and decrement helpers and barriers around transitions, queried by a boolean helper, and combined with atomic context to define handler disabled state; a scoped guard pairs disable with enable.
Remote address untagging requires the memory map lock held as asserted on entry, and page fault guard provides scoped protection by disabling faults on acquisition and re enabling on release.
Page fault handling state is enabled at zero nesting and disabled at positive nesting with paired transitions that move the count up on disable and down on enable.

Unsafe single value and block transfers assume a previously validated region and divert to a caller supplied failure label when the underlying checked operation reports an error; the generic begin helper reduces to an accessibility check, end is a no operation, and save and restore of access state are trivial, with read and write begins aliasing the generic form.

Unsafe helpers must only be used inside a validated access region; use outside such a region risks unchecked user memory access, and failure must transfer to the supplied label without assuming partial progress.

Kernel no fault single value load and store come in architecture assisted and generic accessor based forms, both diverting to a caller label on fault; release store to user orders prior accesses with a full barrier on machines without total store order and a compiler barrier otherwise before delegating to unsafe store.
Scoped helpers acquire a masked pointer when supported or validate the supplied range otherwise, returning the pointer to use, and close the matching read, write or combined scope at exit.
Machine check tolerant copy to kernel is a plain memory copy that always reports success in this configuration.

User access scope moves from closed to open on successful begin or masked acquisition and back to closed on matching end, with failure during open diverting to caller handling and leaving the scope closed.
